correctness.rationale: Conditional ordered normal gaps give exactly the uniform half-angle simplex \(a+b+c=\pi/2\), density \(8/\pi^2\), and the triangle area is the sum of three cotangents. An exact union-of-bands computation gives the \(t^{-1}\) coefficient and the -9/2 unnormalized \(t^{-2}\) term. A uniform middle-edge root expansion contributes \(6\log(\cot\eta)/t^2\), and three exact double-corner integrals contribute \(3[1+2\log(t\eta-1)]/t^2\). With \(\eta=t^{-1/3}\), all discarded terms are \(o(t^{-2})\) and the cutoff disappears. The independently implemented geometric solver and finite-threshold quadrature corroborate the constants but are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The source identifies the total perimeter law of three random tangents as analytically difficult. The theorem supplies a sharp two-term tail with an exact log-enhanced coefficient and constant for the dependent total perimeter/area, quantifying the nontrivial contribution of simultaneous near-parallel tangencies. It sharpens the mere knowledge of infinite first moments, has a natural geometric sampling interpretation, and does not depend on a made-up finite parameter slice.
